_comment: THE TOURS (2026-09-28, TycoonRun.Tour; the first-use lessons 2026-09-29). Each tour plays once a run on its cue (when: first_night = the house tour; first_door, first_shake, first_stir, first_garnish, first_rim = short lessons that start by themselves the first time their mechanic is open and needed). A drag step names where its thing goes (to), and the screen shows a hand carrying it there. {garnish} is the garnish the lesson is about. The first night opens with the hostess walking the player round the room, from the top bar down to the sink, one step at a time; the door is held while she does (the night's clock stands, nobody walks in, the guest's patience does not run). A step is WHAT SHE SAYS (say: one line a key; on a step that waits for the player the last line stays up until it is done), WHAT THE SCREEN POINTS AT (point, a name TycoonHud.Tour resolves: clock, till, bill, stars, house, stool, patience, card, cellar, bottle, bench_bottle, tin_gauge, lid, shaker, serve_key, counter_glass, guest, dirty_glass, cloth, book, tap, corner; empty points at nothing) and WHAT MOVES IT ON (wait, TourWait by name: heard = the plate's key; guest_ready seats the tour's one guest). Slots: {drink} the guest's drink (only after their card is read), {bottle} the next bottle the drink wants. She hands the first job over as the tour ends. Lines are DRAFTS the author rewrites; editing one changes nothing on screen until Tools/loc/data_keys.py and merge_fragments.py --update --write have run - the string table wins over this file. Her name is never written here.

say: There you are, sugar. The doors open at six. Let me walk you round first.
Take your time. Nothing in here moves while I'm talking.
That's the clock. A night runs from six till two in the morning.
When it runs out the door shuts, and whoever's in finishes their drink.
The till. Every drink you sell lands in here, tips and all.
At closing the rent comes back out of it. Hover over the money for tonight's bill.
End three nights running in the red and this room goes dark again.
Those stars are what the street says about us. More stars, more bar.
They open the good bottles, the better pages, the fittings in the market.
Hover over the stars. Hearts are how the drinks went down, diamonds how the room feels.
The night is filed at the lower of the two, so mind both.
Here's your first guest. Give them a second to make up their mind.
That bar over their head is patience. Once it's gone, so are they.
Tonight, while I'm showing you round, it waits for you. After that it won't.
Nobody tells you what they want. Click their stool and read the card.
Name, age, and the drink they came for. The order only ever lives on the card.
The fine print will matter later. Tonight, everybody's who they say they are.
Hover over the drink's name and its recipe comes up beside it.
Hold still a moment and it settles. The pin keeps it up on the screen while you work.
Click anywhere off the card to put it away. The pinned recipe stays.
Every drink starts in the cellar under the counter. Open it up.
{drink} starts with {bottle}. Take it off the shelf.
Grab the bottle and tip it over the tin. The higher you lift it, the faster it runs.
The tin shows what's in it. The book lights the box each bottle lands in.
Close is fine tonight. Dead on is what the tips are for.
The list on the left walks you through the drink. Each step ticks off as you do it.
Pour it wrong? The bin tips the tin out. It costs a little, so aim first.
Now the {bottle}. Back to the bar with the arrow, take it from the cellar and pour it in.
This one is built. No shaking, just drag the lid onto the tin.
Grab the tin and tip it over the glass. Whatever misses the glass is gone.
Happy with it? SERVE IT puts the glass on the counter.
Now hand it over. Drag the glass to your guest, or just click them.
Watch their face. That's the review, and it goes into the stars.
They pay when they get up. The tip rides on speed, craft and a good fill.
Now let them finish. Nobody likes being rushed.
They leave the glass behind, and a stool with a dirty glass in front of it seats nobody.
Drag that glass into the sink.
And that ring on the wood. A dirty counter costs you the room's diamonds.
Grab the cloth and rub it out.
Forgot how a drink goes? The menu on the counter has every page we pour.
The night crawls while it's open, but it never stops. Click off the book to close it.
That's the tap. Beer is a craft of its own. I'll show you when somebody asks.
Escape pauses the night. The settings are in there.
When the door shuts, the night's slip comes up, then the market: bottles, pages and fittings.
That's the job, sugar. The door is yours.
One more thing before I let you work.
The door is yours now, sugar. Check the age: under twenty, they don't drink here.
Look at the card itself. A flag that isn't their country, a face that isn't theirs, a card that looks drawn: that's a fake.
KICK shows them the door. Get it right and the city thanks you at closing.
Pour for a kid and you pay the fine. Throw out an honest face and you lose a guest.
This one is shaken. It wants ice and air through it, not a spoon.
Cap it first. Drag the lid onto the tin.
Now grab the tin, hold the button and shake it back and forth until the MIX column fills.
That's a shake. Over to the glass, same as before.
This one is stirred, not shaken. Take the spoon and work circles over the open tin.
Silk, not foam. Cap it and take it over.
They asked for {garnish}. Drag it from its dish onto the glass.
Little things. They tip for little things. Now hand it over.
They want {garnish}. Hold the dish and run it once round the rim of the glass.
That's a rim. Now hand it over.
